evidence.description: Dispatch updates stored state immediately but schedules notification delivery in an unawaited MainActor task.
Subscription and unsubscription also schedule unawaited tasks rather than completing their observer operations before returning.

candidates.explanation: The actor serializes task creation, not completion of the notification and observer operations. Callers can finish awaiting subscribe or unsubscribe while the corresponding registration change is still pending. The independently scheduled tasks also provide no explicit ordering guarantee between registration, removal, and notification delivery, allowing missed notifications or callbacks after unsubscription has returned.
candidates.title: Unstructured tasks disconnect observer operations from actor ordering

evidence.description: Dispatch reads and writes state using the separate windowUUID argument.
The notification identifies the window using that same argument.
The reducer constructs the stored state using action.windowUUID instead.

candidates.explanation: The public dispatch method accepts a window identifier both directly and inside the action without checking that they match. Different values cause a state identifying one window to be stored under another window's key and broadcast with that other identifier. This breaks the consistency of the per-window state mapping and can combine one window's existing state with another window's action.
candidates.title: Dispatch accepts conflicting window identifiers
